description: Eliware Test deterministic validation and enforcement directive.

authoritativeFor: Deterministic enforcement of applicable repository conventions.
Deterministic test, coverage, lint, package-check, and validation behavior.
notAuthoritativeFor: Semantic AI review, human acceptance decisions, release authorization, deployment, or operations.

crosslinks.authoritativeFor: Repository authority and the E-18 namespace.
Repository conventions enforced by this package.

dos: Enforce every applicable repository convention that can be validated deterministically, either fully or through its deterministically verifiable requirements.
Return only pass or fail for each enforced check while preserving distinct process exit codes for distinct failure categories.
Skip entirely any convention directive that cannot be enforced even partially through deterministic repository, configuration, filesystem, process, or test evidence.
Store each deterministic check in src/checks/<profile>/<id>.mjs, where the filename identifies the exact convention directive ID.
Use package.json.eliware.conventions to determine the convention version, applied convention groups, and exact exempted rule IDs.
Preserve the deterministically enforceable behavior of the previous eliware-test release unless it conflicts with this directive or the v8 conventions.
Keep the public consumer interface at the eliware-test CLI and keep check modules, orchestrators, diagnostics, and utilities as separate implementation responsibilities.
donts: Do not infer which convention groups apply from project files, dependencies, entrypoints, or implementation patterns.
Do not create enforcement modules for requirements that require semantic judgment, owner approval, human acceptance, or live operational evidence.
Do not use profiles to force repositories into a single project type; apply groups and exemptions must be explicitly declared in package.json.
Do not silently pass missing, malformed, duplicate, unknown, or unexpectedly skipped checks.
Do not expose internal check modules as a consumer runtime API.
Do not weaken an explicit Eliware convention through an inferred exception or an undocumented command-line flag.
Do not provide project-specific smoke, integration, regression, end-to-end, deployment, release, or live-operational workflows.
Do not provide coverage merging, coverage backup or restoration, worktree concurrency coordination, comprehensive secret redaction, or a supported runtime-library embedding API.

dos: Keep the eliware-test CLI as a thin public entrypoint that delegates validation to focused orchestrators.
donts: Do not make consumers import internal check, orchestrator, diagnostic, or utility modules.

dos: Support help and version terminal modes and report the installed package version from package.json.
Support lint, format, format-check, debug-timing, coverage, focused-test, in-band, and documented enforcement options according to the CLI contract.
Validate wrapper-owned arguments before starting validation and forward unrelated Jest arguments unchanged.
donts: Do not require consumers to know internal module paths or structured toolkit seams.

dos: Use Node child-process APIs and argument arrays for subprocess execution.

Run the validation lifecycle in the documented order: workspace policy, conventions, argument and architecture validation, Jest with coverage, coverage evaluation, lint, monolith enforcement, and configured package checks.
Run post-test stages after coverage failure so one invocation reports all actionable diagnostics.
donts: Do not depend on shell pipelines, shell quoting, grep, or platform-specific executable names.

dos: Keep successful output concise and preserve useful test, lint, coverage, and package diagnostics.
Use stable exit categories for workspace setup, policy, arguments, focused paths, coverage, tests, lint, monoliths, architecture, package scripts, conventions, and internal failures.
Return the highest applicable post-test failure code after all applicable post-test stages complete.
donts: Do not expose internal implementation results as a second consumer API.

dos: Read the convention version, applied groups, and exemptions from package.json.eliware.conventions before discovering checks.
donts: Do not infer applicability from dependencies, files, scripts, entrypoints, or runtime behavior.

dos: Always evaluate the general check group and evaluate each explicitly applied group once.
donts: Do not silently ignore an applied group or duplicate a selected check.

dos: Skip only exact exempted rule IDs and validate exemption records before execution.
donts: Do not use broad, implicit, or profile-wide exemptions when an individual rule is intended.

dos: Reject unsupported convention versions, unknown groups, unknown rules, malformed configuration, and duplicate IDs.
donts: Do not convert configuration errors into a passing result.

dos: Discover checks from src/checks/<profile>/ directories selected by the repository configuration.
donts: Do not mix check modules with orchestrators, utilities, diagnostics, or other implementation modules.

dos: Use src/checks/<profile>/<id>.mjs as the canonical location for deterministic convention checks.
donts: Do not create check modules for requirements that cannot be partially validated deterministically.

dos: Require check filenames, exported IDs, and discovered IDs to match exactly.
donts: Do not let one module silently represent multiple unrelated directive IDs.

dos: Give every check one exact convention directive ID and require every result to identify that same ID.
donts: Do not allow a check to silently cover multiple unrelated directives or return an indeterminate result.

dos: Return pass or fail with a stable rule ID and actionable diagnostic text.
Treat statements, branches, functions, and lines as independent coverage requirements.
Treat zero-valued coverage metrics, malformed coverage evidence, missing usable evidence, and unmapped required files as failures.
donts: Do not return review, warning, skipped, or unknown as validation outcomes.

dos: Run deterministic checks against a shared repository context and keep filesystem and process inputs bounded.

Discover source and test trees deterministically, exclude dependency, VCS, coverage, build, distribution, and test-result directories, and fail bounded traversal overflow rather than continuing unbounded discovery.
Normalize workspace paths, bound child output, deduplicate repeated diagnostics, and keep debug timing in memory.
donts: Do not make check results depend on hidden mutable state or undocumented inference.

dos: Aggregate all selected check results and preserve actionable diagnostics while returning a deterministic process result.
donts: Do not treat an unknown group, missing check, malformed check, or invalid exemption as a successful validation.

dos: Run Jest in-band by default, support an explicit --no-runInBand diagnostic opt-out, collect coverage, and preserve focused-path behavior.
Recognize conventional test paths, reject missing paths before Jest, use strict runTestsByPath selection when paths are present, and never fall back silently to the full suite.
Scope coverage to an unambiguous mirrored source file for focused runs and use broad producer-defined coverage for unmappable runs.
donts: Do not silently fall back to the full suite when a requested focused path is missing.

dos: Run Oxlint with warnings denied and enforce the existing Istanbul-ignore policy.
Scan applicable files for Istanbul ignore directives and report executable files hidden by coverage exclusions.
Preserve the explicit --lint behavior and do not duplicate successful lint output in the integrated pipeline.
donts: Do not treat warning-level lint findings or executable-code ignore comments as successful validation.

dos: Validate usable JSON and text coverage evidence, fail closed on gaps, and support the explicit 100x4 diagnostic opt-out.
Use fixed coverage candidate precedence, reject unsafe or structurally inconsistent counters, fall back to the Jest text report when JSON is unusable, and treat fresh malformed evidence as failure.
Keep --ignore-100x4 limited to enforcement; tests, coverage collection, lint, package checks, and other validation still run.
donts: Do not let the coverage opt-out skip tests, lint, coverage collection, or other checks.

dos: Keep deterministic repository checks, test execution, coverage enforcement, linting, package checks, and diagnostics in separately testable modules.
donts: Do not add a new responsibility to an existing module when a focused module can own it.

dos: Validate required repository paths, package metadata, documentation indexes, local links, examples, environment templates, and applicable CI metadata.
Require README.md, AGENTS.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md, docs/, specs/, examples/, and .env.example unless an exact documented path exception applies.

Validate package identity, Node runtime metadata, scripts, license, README links, specification indexes, example navigation, local Markdown links, safe environment placeholders, and documentation for source-referenced environment variables.
Require scripts.test to invoke eliware-test unless the repository has an exact approved exemption for its self-hosting arrangement.
donts: Do not execute examples or treat prose quality as deterministic validation evidence.

dos: Exclude dependency, VCS, coverage, build, distribution, test-result, and other configured generated paths from discovery.
Warn rather than fail for a missing .gitignore when the convention defines that behavior, while still validating existing policy files.
Treat generated-file markers as size-policy exemptions only; they do not exempt files from mapping, coverage, or Istanbul policy.
donts: Do not let exclusions conceal source, test, coverage, or convention failures in included files.

dos: Validate strict src/**/*.mjs to tests/**/*.test.mjs architecture mapping, enforce source files at 100 lines or fewer and test files at 200 lines or fewer, and recognize pure barrels and generated files only under documented rules.
Keep mapping discovery, focused-path discovery, monolith discovery, and workspace-policy discovery as separate bounded policies.
donts: Do not treat a size exemption as an exemption from coverage, mapping, or other policy checks.

dos: Retain deterministic behavior explicitly adopted by v8 while implementing the v8 interface natively.
donts: Do not add compatibility shims or preserve obsolete interfaces merely because their old implementation is being replaced.

dos: Run defined audit, pack, build, and typecheck scripts after the core validation stages without invoking the consumer test script recursively.
Skip absent optional scripts, reject empty or invalid defined scripts, run valid scripts through the supported npm and Node launcher contract, and normalize failures to the package-check category.
donts: Do not treat a missing npm launcher, invalid script, or nonzero package script as success.

dos: Keep package metadata, lockfiles, README, release notes, packed files, and CI evidence synchronized.
Verify npm pack contents against the package files allowlist, require the supported CLI bin, and preserve the intentional absence of exports and declaration surfaces when applicable.
Require Node 26-compatible native ESM package behavior and the shared Jest/Oxlint runtime dependencies.
donts: Do not publish, tag, push, deploy, or release as an implicit side effect of validation.

dos: Preserve native v8 behavior, self-hosting support, bounded diagnostics, and platform-specific npm launch behavior.
Keep consumers responsible for specialized smoke, integration, regression, and end-to-end workflows; keep TagIt responsible for release state and CodeScope responsible for semantic review.
Require explicit authorization outside this package before tagging, publishing, pushing, deploying, synchronizing, or performing destructive actions.
donts: Do not promise unsupported package managers, runtime layouts, concurrency models, or live operational guarantees.
